title: Who Dared Pull the Emperor's Mustache? (PT)
summary: Akbar asks his ministers what punishment fits a scoundrel who dared pull his royal mustache. Courtiers demand execution, but Birbal suggests sweetmeats.
full_text:
One morning, Emperor Akbar arrived at the Diwan-i-Khas with a stern, brooding expression. The courtiers sat in nervous silence, wondering what crisis of state had troubled their sovereign.

Suddenly, Akbar slammed his fist upon the arm of the golden throne and demanded:

'My lords and counselors! Tell me at once: what punishment does a traitor deserve who had the brazen audacity to pull the royal mustache of the Emperor of Hindustan?'

The courtiers gasped in sheer horror! To touch the Emperor's body was high treason; to pull his mustache was an unforgivable sacrilege!

One bloodthirsty general jumped to his feet: 'Sire! He should be beheaded immediately, and his head mounted on a spike at the Delhi Gate!'

The chief magistrate shouted: 'He should be flayed alive and trampled under the feet of war elephants!'

The royal treasurer added: 'His entire family should be banished and his house razed to the ground!'

Every nobleman in the hall competed to propose the most gruesome, agonizing execution.

Only Birbal sat quietly in his seat, smiling with gentle amusement.

Akbar turned his piercing gaze toward Birbal: 'And you, Birbal? You sit there smiling! What punishment do you prescribe for the culprit who pulled my mustache?'

Birbal stepped forward, bowed low, and answered in a warm, melodic voice:

'Your Majesty, I propose that the culprit be rewarded with an enormous silver bowl overflowing with the sweetest, richest saffron jalebis and pistachios!'

The courtiers were stunned into dead silence. Some whispered that Birbal had finally committed treason!

Akbar smiled: 'Birbal, why do you suggest sweetmeats for such a terrible offense?'

Birbal laughed softly:

'Sire, who in all of Hindustan would have the courage or opportunity to reach up and pull the Emperor's mustache, except for your beloved little grandson, Prince Khurram, while playing upon your royal lap this morning?

'No enemy or traitor could ever get close enough to touch a single hair on your face! Only an innocent child who loves you with all his heart could pull your mustache, and for such love, sweetmeats are the only proper reward!'

Akbar threw back his head and laughed with overflowing delight, confessing that his little grandson had indeed tugged his mustache while playing that morning. Akbar embraced Birbal, praising his matchless understanding of human reality.
